title: MacPaw and Liquid AI bring private, offline inference to desktop apps
friendlyTitle: MacPaw is building AI that works on your device
summary: MacPaw is working with Liquid AI on Elix, an on-device inference and local-memory system for its Eney assistant. The companies plan to make the stack available to Setapp developers, alongside access to cloud models and credit-based pricing for AI features.
friendlySummary: MacPaw and Liquid AI are making a local system for the Eney assistant and, later, other Setapp developers. It can work offline and keep more data on the device.
whyItMatters: Local processing can keep personal context on the device, work without an internet connection and reduce recurring cloud inference costs. Developers will still need to balance those benefits against model quality, battery use, hardware compatibility and update complexity.
friendlyWhyItMatters: Local AI can be more private and may cost less to run, but it must still work well on ordinary computers.
